attributes.tool.tavily_map: Map and discover the structure of a website by finding all its URLs and pages. CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. provides cybersecurity solutions in the United States and internationally. Its unified platform provides cloud-delivered protection of endpoints, cloud workloads, identity, and data through a software as a service (SaaS) subscription-based model. The company offers corporate endpoint and cloud workload security, managed security, security and vulnerability management, IT operations management, identity protection, threat intelligence, data protection, SaaS security posture management, and AI powered workflow automation, and securing generative AI workload services, as well as security orchestration, automation, and response; and security information and event management, and log management services. It primarily sells subscriptions to its Falcon platform and cloud modules. CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. was incorporated in 2011 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas.

Strong Growth, Sticky Revenue, and a Critical Industry Tailwind

If you’ve been paying attention to the headlines lately, you’ll notice something, cyberattacks aren’t slowing down. In fact, they’re multiplying.

From ransomware hitting hospitals to phishing campaigns targeting Fortune 500s, the cost of being unprepared is higher than ever.

Cybersecurity isn’t getting cut. If anything, it’s the last line item on the list, spending will only rise. It’s that simple.

Enter CrowdStrike.

CrowdStrike is a leader in cybersecurity. It specializes in endpoint security, threat intelligence and cyber attack response services. They’re not just selling software; they’re selling protection that companies cannot aff

ord to lose.

CrowdStrike’s Falcon platform is built in the cloud, powered by AI, and designed to catch threats before they even become headlines. That’s why businesses from small firms to Fortune 500s are paying to protect themselves, and they keep paying. Once you’re in the CrowdStrike ecosystem, you rarely leave.

That group currently includes 300 of the Fortune 500 companies. 42 of the 50 U.S. states.

CrowdStrike is more than a software company, it’s a backbone of modern business security. With massive secular tailwinds, sticky recurring revenue, expanding opportunities, and a defensible moat. CrowdStrike isn’t just a growth stock, it’s a mission-critical one.

**The Case for CrowdStrike**

*   **Mission-Critical Spend** – Cybersecurity budgets are sticky. Companies may renegotiate SaaS contracts or trim cloud usage, but they don’t roll the dice on protection. That gives CrowdStrike unusually durable demand, even in downturns. 
*   **Best-in-Class Platform** – The Falcon platform is cloud-native and AI-driven, recognized as one of the top endpoint protection tools in the industry. 
*   **Compounding Revenue** – Subscription revenue means predictable growth. They project a $10 billion ARR goal by 2031 and $20 billion ARR projection by 2036. Over 90% of their revenue is subscription based. 

- **Retention Holding Up –** With an over 115% net retention, existing customers are expanding their usage and spending more every year.

*   **Growing Market** – From endpoint protection to cloud, identity, and XDR, CrowdStrike’s management sees a total addressable market (TAM) of $300 billion by 2029. That’s up from $116 billion this year. 
*   **Growth + Profitability** – Rare among high-growth names, CrowdStrike is GAAP profitable with strong free cash flow, giving them room to invest aggressively while still delivering to shareholders. They’ve maintained an over 73% gross profit margin. 
*   **A Data-Driven Moat** – The “threat graph” analyzes trillions of events daily. More data = better AI = better protection. This flywheel effect is incredibly hard for competitors to replicate. 

CrowdStrike pairs rapid revenue growth and high customer retention with expanding market opportunities, founder-led execution, strong profitability, and a defensible moat.

In today’s world, I feel that I to have a horse in the cybersecurity space. CrowdStrike is my horse.

It has been and is still one of my favorite long-term growth stocks in the entire stock market. I’ve been long since I started my position back in September 2020. My last sale where I trimmed my position was in January 2022.

I’ve held every share since and have continued to buy more during pullbacks.

On any market pullback, this is the first name on my buy list.

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. provides cybersecurity solutions in the United States and internationally. Its unified platform provides cloud-delivered protection of endpoints, cloud workloads, identity, and data through a software as a service (SaaS) subscription-based model. The company offers corporate endpoint and cloud workload security, managed security, security and vulnerability management, IT operations management, identity protection, threat intelligence, data protection, SaaS security posture management, and AI powered workflow automation, and securing generative AI workload services, as well as security orchestration, automation, and response; and security information and event management, and log management services. It primarily sells subscriptions to its Falcon platform and cloud modules. CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. was incorporated in 2011 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas.

The Cybersecurity Stock To Own
------------------------------

Strong Growth, Sticky Revenue, and a Critical Industry Tailwind

If you’ve been paying attention to the headlines lately, you’ll notice something, cyberattacks aren’t slowing down. In fact, they’re multiplying.

From ransomware hitting hospitals to phishing campaigns targeting Fortune 500s, the cost of being unprepared is higher than ever.

Cybersecurity isn’t getting cut. If anything, it’s the last line item on the list, spending will only rise. It’s that simple.

Enter CrowdStrike.

CrowdStrike is a leader in cybersecurity. It specializes in endpoint security, threat intelligence and cyber attack response services. They’re not just selling software; they’re selling protection that companies cannot aff

ord to lose.

CrowdStrike’s Falcon platform is built in the cloud, powered by AI, and designed to catch threats before they even become headlines. That’s why businesses from small firms to Fortune 500s are paying to protect themselves, and they keep paying. Once you’re in the CrowdStrike ecosystem, you rarely leave.

That group currently includes 300 of the Fortune 500 companies. 42 of the 50 U.S. states.

CrowdStrike is more than a software company, it’s a backbone of modern business security. With massive secular tailwinds, sticky recurring revenue, expanding opportunities, and a defensible moat. CrowdStrike isn’t just a growth stock, it’s a mission-critical one.

**The Case for CrowdStrike**

*   **Mission-Critical Spend** – Cybersecurity budgets are sticky. Companies may renegotiate SaaS contracts or trim cloud usage, but they don’t roll the dice on protection. That gives CrowdStrike unusually durable demand, even in downturns. 
*   **Best-in-Class Platform** – The Falcon platform is cloud-native and AI-driven, recognized as one of the top endpoint protection tools in the industry. 
*   **Compounding Revenue** – Subscription revenue means predictable growth. They project a $10 billion ARR goal by 2031 and $20 billion ARR projection by 2036. Over 90% of their revenue is subscription based. 

- **Retention Holding Up –** With an over 115% net retention, existing customers are expanding their usage and spending more every year.

*   **Growing Market** – From endpoint protection to cloud, identity, and XDR, CrowdStrike’s management sees a total addressable market (TAM) of $300 billion by 2029. That’s up from $116 billion this year. 
*   **Growth + Profitability** – Rare among high-growth names, CrowdStrike is GAAP profitable with strong free cash flow, giving them room to invest aggressively while still delivering to shareholders. They’ve maintained an over 73% gross profit margin. 
*   **A Data-Driven Moat** – The “threat graph” analyzes trillions of events daily. More data = better AI = better protection. This flywheel effect is incredibly hard for competitors to replicate. 

CrowdStrike pairs rapid revenue growth and high customer retention with expanding market opportunities, founder-led execution, strong profitability, and a defensible moat.

In today’s world, I feel that I to have a horse in the cybersecurity space. CrowdStrike is my horse.

It has been and is still one of my favorite long-term growth stocks in the entire stock market. I’ve been long since I started my position back in September 2020. My last sale where I trimmed my position was in January 2022.

I’ve held every share since and have continued to buy more during pullbacks.

On any market pullback, this is the first name on my buy list.

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. provides cybersecurity solutions in the United States and internationally. Its unified platform provides cloud-delivered protection of endpoints, cloud workloads, identity, and data through a software as a service (SaaS) subscription-based model. The company offers corporate endpoint and cloud workload security, managed security, security and vulnerability management, IT operations management, identity protection, threat intelligence, data protection, SaaS security posture management, and AI powered workflow automation, and securing generative AI workload services, as well as security orchestration, automation, and response; and security information and event management, and log management services. It primarily sells subscriptions to its Falcon platform and cloud modules. CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. was incorporated in 2011 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas.

The Cybersecurity Stock To Own
------------------------------

Strong Growth, Sticky Revenue, and a Critical Industry Tailwind

If you’ve been paying attention to the headlines lately, you’ll notice something, cyberattacks aren’t slowing down. In fact, they’re multiplying.

From ransomware hitting hospitals to phishing campaigns targeting Fortune 500s, the cost of being unprepared is higher than ever.

Cybersecurity isn’t getting cut. If anything, it’s the last line item on the list, spending will only rise. It’s that simple.

Enter CrowdStrike.

CrowdStrike is a leader in cybersecurity. It specializes in endpoint security, threat intelligence and cyber attack response services. They’re not just selling software; they’re selling protection that companies cannot aff

ord to lose.

CrowdStrike’s Falcon platform is built in the cloud, powered by AI, and designed to catch threats before they even become headlines. That’s why businesses from small firms to Fortune 500s are paying to protect themselves, and they keep paying. Once you’re in the CrowdStrike ecosystem, you rarely leave.

That group currently includes 300 of the Fortune 500 companies. 42 of the 50 U.S. states.

CrowdStrike is more than a software company, it’s a backbone of modern business security. With massive secular tailwinds, sticky recurring revenue, expanding opportunities, and a defensible moat. CrowdStrike isn’t just a growth stock, it’s a mission-critical one.

**The Case for CrowdStrike**

*   **Mission-Critical Spend** – Cybersecurity budgets are sticky. Companies may renegotiate SaaS contracts or trim cloud usage, but they don’t roll the dice on protection. That gives CrowdStrike unusually durable demand, even in downturns. 
*   **Best-in-Class Platform** – The Falcon platform is cloud-native and AI-driven, recognized as one of the top endpoint protection tools in the industry. 
*   **Compounding Revenue** – Subscription revenue means predictable growth. They project a $10 billion ARR goal by 2031 and $20 billion ARR projection by 2036. Over 90% of their revenue is subscription based. 

- **Retention Holding Up –** With an over 115% net retention, existing customers are expanding their usage and spending more every year.

*   **Growing Market** – From endpoint protection to cloud, identity, and XDR, CrowdStrike’s management sees a total addressable market (TAM) of $300 billion by 2029. That’s up from $116 billion this year. 
*   **Growth + Profitability** – Rare among high-growth names, CrowdStrike is GAAP profitable with strong free cash flow, giving them room to invest aggressively while still delivering to shareholders. They’ve maintained an over 73% gross profit margin. 
*   **A Data-Driven Moat** – The “threat graph” analyzes trillions of events daily. More data = better AI = better protection. This flywheel effect is incredibly hard for competitors to replicate. 

CrowdStrike pairs rapid revenue growth and high customer retention with expanding market opportunities, founder-led execution, strong profitability, and a defensible moat.

In today’s world, I feel that I to have a horse in the cybersecurity space. CrowdStrike is my horse.

It has been and is still one of my favorite long-term growth stocks in the entire stock market. I’ve been long since I started my position back in September 2020. My last sale where I trimmed my position was in January 2022.

I’ve held every share since and have continued to buy more during pullbacks.

On any market pullback, this is the first name on my buy list.

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. provides cybersecurity solutions in the United States and internationally. Its unified platform provides cloud-delivered protection of endpoints, cloud workloads, identity, and data through a software as a service (SaaS) subscription-based model. The company offers corporate endpoint and cloud workload security, managed security, security and vulnerability management, IT operations management, identity protection, threat intelligence, data protection, SaaS security posture management, and AI powered workflow automation, and securing generative AI workload services, as well as security orchestration, automation, and response; and security information and event management, and log management services. It primarily sells subscriptions to its Falcon platform and cloud modules. CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. was incorporated in 2011 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas.

The Cybersecurity Stock To Own
------------------------------

Strong Growth, Sticky Revenue, and a Critical Industry Tailwind

If you’ve been paying attention to the headlines lately, you’ll notice something, cyberattacks aren’t slowing down. In fact, they’re multiplying.

From ransomware hitting hospitals to phishing campaigns targeting Fortune 500s, the cost of being unprepared is higher than ever.

Cybersecurity isn’t getting cut. If anything, it’s the last line item on the list, spending will only rise. It’s that simple.

Enter CrowdStrike.

CrowdStrike is a leader in cybersecurity. It specializes in endpoint security, threat intelligence and cyber attack response services. They’re not just selling software; they’re selling protection that companies cannot aff

ord to lose.

CrowdStrike’s Falcon platform is built in the cloud, powered by AI, and designed to catch threats before they even become headlines. That’s why businesses from small firms to Fortune 500s are paying to protect themselves, and they keep paying. Once you’re in the CrowdStrike ecosystem, you rarely leave.

That group currently includes 300 of the Fortune 500 companies. 42 of the 50 U.S. states.

CrowdStrike is more than a software company, it’s a backbone of modern business security. With massive secular tailwinds, sticky recurring revenue, expanding opportunities, and a defensible moat. CrowdStrike isn’t just a growth stock, it’s a mission-critical one.

**The Case for CrowdStrike**

*   **Mission-Critical Spend** – Cybersecurity budgets are sticky. Companies may renegotiate SaaS contracts or trim cloud usage, but they don’t roll the dice on protection. That gives CrowdStrike unusually durable demand, even in downturns. 
*   **Best-in-Class Platform** – The Falcon platform is cloud-native and AI-driven, recognized as one of the top endpoint protection tools in the industry. 
*   **Compounding Revenue** – Subscription revenue means predictable growth. They project a $10 billion ARR goal by 2031 and $20 billion ARR projection by 2036. Over 90% of their revenue is subscription based. 

- **Retention Holding Up –** With an over 115% net retention, existing customers are expanding their usage and spending more every year.

*   **Growing Market** – From endpoint protection to cloud, identity, and XDR, CrowdStrike’s management sees a total addressable market (TAM) of $300 billion by 2029. That’s up from $116 billion this year. 
*   **Growth + Profitability** – Rare among high-growth names, CrowdStrike is GAAP profitable with strong free cash flow, giving them room to invest aggressively while still delivering to shareholders. They’ve maintained an over 73% gross profit margin. 
*   **A Data-Driven Moat** – The “threat graph” analyzes trillions of events daily. More data = better AI = better protection. This flywheel effect is incredibly hard for competitors to replicate. 

CrowdStrike pairs rapid revenue growth and high customer retention with expanding market opportunities, founder-led execution, strong profitability, and a defensible moat.

In today’s world, I feel that I to have a horse in the cybersecurity space. CrowdStrike is my horse.

It has been and is still one of my favorite long-term growth stocks in the entire stock market. I’ve been long since I started my position back in September 2020. My last sale where I trimmed my position was in January 2022.

I’ve held every share since and have continued to buy more during pullbacks.

On any market pullback, this is the first name on my buy list.

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. provides cybersecurity solutions in the United States and internationally. Its unified platform provides cloud-delivered protection of endpoints, cloud workloads, identity, and data through a software as a service (SaaS) subscription-based model. The company offers corporate endpoint and cloud workload security, managed security, security and vulnerability management, IT operations management, identity protection, threat intelligence, data protection, SaaS security posture management, and AI powered workflow automation, and securing generative AI workload services, as well as security orchestration, automation, and response; and security information and event management, and log management services. It primarily sells subscriptions to its Falcon platform and cloud modules. CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. was incorporated in 2011 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas.

Cybersecurity isn’t getting cut. If anything, it’s the last line item on the list, spending will only rise. It’s that simple.

Enter CrowdStrike.

CrowdStrike is a leader in cybersecurity. It specializes in endpoint security, threat intelligence and cyber attack response services. They’re not just selling software; they’re selling protection that companies cannot aff

ord to lose.

CrowdStrike’s Falcon platform is built in the cloud, powered by AI, and designed to catch threats before they even become headlines. That’s why businesses from small firms to Fortune 500s are paying to protect themselves, and they keep paying. Once you’re in the CrowdStrike ecosystem, you rarely leave.

That group currently includes 300 of the Fortune 500 companies. 42 of the 50 U.S. states.

CrowdStrike is more than a software company, it’s a backbone of modern business security. With massive secular tailwinds, sticky recurring revenue, expanding opportunities, and a defensible moat. CrowdStrike isn’t just a growth stock, it’s a mission-critical one.

**The Case for CrowdStrike**

*   **Mission-Critical Spend** – Cybersecurity budgets are sticky. Companies may renegotiate SaaS contracts or trim cloud usage, but they don’t roll the dice on protection. That gives CrowdStrike unusually durable demand, even in downturns. 
*   **Best-in-Class Platform** – The Falcon platform is cloud-native and AI-driven, recognized as one of the top endpoint protection tools in the industry. 
*   **Compounding Revenue** – Subscription revenue means predictable growth. They project a $10 billion ARR goal by 2031 and $20 billion ARR projection by 2036. Over 90% of their revenue is subscription based. 

- **Retention Holding Up –** With an over 115% net retention, existing customers are expanding their usage and spending more every year.

*   **Growing Market** – From endpoint protection to cloud, identity, and XDR, CrowdStrike’s management sees a total addressable market (TAM) of $300 billion by 2029. That’s up from $116 billion this year. 
*   **Growth + Profitability** – Rare among high-growth names, CrowdStrike is GAAP profitable with strong free cash flow, giving them room to invest aggressively while still delivering to shareholders. They’ve maintained an over 73% gross profit margin. 
*   **A Data-Driven Moat** – The “threat graph” analyzes trillions of events daily. More data = better AI = better protection. This flywheel effect is incredibly hard for competitors to replicate. 

CrowdStrike pairs rapid revenue growth and high customer retention with expanding market opportunities, founder-led execution, strong profitability, and a defensible moat.

In today’s world, I feel that I to have a horse in the cybersecurity space. CrowdStrike is my horse.

It has been and is still one of my favorite long-term growth stocks in the entire stock market. I’ve been long since I started my position back in September 2020. My last sale where I trimmed my position was in January 2022.

I’ve held every share since and have continued to buy more during pullbacks.

On any market pullback, this is the first name on my buy list.

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. provides cybersecurity solutions in the United States and internationally. Its unified platform provides cloud-delivered protection of endpoints, cloud workloads, identity, and data through a software as a service (SaaS) subscription-based model. The company offers corporate endpoint and cloud workload security, managed security, security and vulnerability management, IT operations management, identity protection, threat intelligence, data protection, SaaS security posture management, and AI powered workflow automation, and securing generative AI workload services, as well as security orchestration, automation, and response; and security information and event management, and log management services. It primarily sells subscriptions to its Falcon platform and cloud modules. CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. was incorporated in 2011 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas.

The Cybersecurity Stock To Own
------------------------------

Strong Growth, Sticky Revenue, and a Critical Industry Tailwind

If you’ve been paying attention to the headlines lately, you’ll notice something, cyberattacks aren’t slowing down. In fact, they’re multiplying.

From ransomware hitting hospitals to phishing campaigns targeting Fortune 500s, the cost of being unprepared is higher than ever.

Cybersecurity isn’t getting cut. If anything, it’s the last line item on the list, spending will only rise. It’s that simple.

Enter CrowdStrike.

CrowdStrike is a leader in cybersecurity. It specializes in endpoint security, threat intelligence and cyber attack response services. They’re not just selling software; they’re selling protection that companies cannot aff

ord to lose.

CrowdStrike’s Falcon platform is built in the cloud, powered by AI, and designed to catch threats before they even become headlines. That’s why businesses from small firms to Fortune 500s are paying to protect themselves, and they keep paying. Once you’re in the CrowdStrike ecosystem, you rarely leave.

That group currently includes 300 of the Fortune 500 companies. 42 of the 50 U.S. states.

CrowdStrike is more than a software company, it’s a backbone of modern business security. With massive secular tailwinds, sticky recurring revenue, expanding opportunities, and a defensible moat. CrowdStrike isn’t just a growth stock, it’s a mission-critical one.

**The Case for CrowdStrike**

*   **Mission-Critical Spend** – Cybersecurity budgets are sticky. Companies may renegotiate SaaS contracts or trim cloud usage, but they don’t roll the dice on protection. That gives CrowdStrike unusually durable demand, even in downturns. 
*   **Best-in-Class Platform** – The Falcon platform is cloud-native and AI-driven, recognized as one of the top endpoint protection tools in the industry. 
*   **Compounding Revenue** – Subscription revenue means predictable growth. They project a $10 billion ARR goal by 2031 and $20 billion ARR projection by 2036. Over 90% of their revenue is subscription based. 

- **Retention Holding Up –** With an over 115% net retention, existing customers are expanding their usage and spending more every year.

*   **Growing Market** – From endpoint protection to cloud, identity, and XDR, CrowdStrike’s management sees a total addressable market (TAM) of $300 billion by 2029. That’s up from $116 billion this year. 
*   **Growth + Profitability** – Rare among high-growth names, CrowdStrike is GAAP profitable with strong free cash flow, giving them room to invest aggressively while still delivering to shareholders. They’ve maintained an over 73% gross profit margin. 
*   **A Data-Driven Moat** – The “threat graph” analyzes trillions of events daily. More data = better AI = better protection. This flywheel effect is incredibly hard for competitors to replicate. 

CrowdStrike pairs rapid revenue growth and high customer retention with expanding market opportunities, founder-led execution, strong profitability, and a defensible moat.

In today’s world, I feel that I to have a horse in the cybersecurity space. CrowdStrike is my horse.

It has been and is still one of my favorite long-term growth stocks in the entire stock market. I’ve been long since I started my position back in September 2020. My last sale where I trimmed my position was in January 2022.

I’ve held every share since and have continued to buy more during pullbacks.

On any market pullback, this is the first name on my buy list.

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. provides cybersecurity solutions in the United States and internationally. Its unified platform provides cloud-delivered protection of endpoints, cloud workloads, identity, and data through a software as a service (SaaS) subscription-based model. The company offers corporate endpoint and cloud workload security, managed security, security and vulnerability management, IT operations management, identity protection, threat intelligence, data protection, SaaS security posture management, and AI powered workflow automation, and securing generative AI workload services, as well as security orchestration, automation, and response; and security information and event management, and log management services. It primarily sells subscriptions to its Falcon platform and cloud modules. CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. was incorporated in 2011 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas.

The Cybersecurity Stock To Own
------------------------------

Strong Growth, Sticky Revenue, and a Critical Industry Tailwind

If you’ve been paying attention to the headlines lately, you’ll notice something, cyberattacks aren’t slowing down. In fact, they’re multiplying.

From ransomware hitting hospitals to phishing campaigns targeting Fortune 500s, the cost of being unprepared is higher than ever.

Cybersecurity isn’t getting cut. If anything, it’s the last line item on the list, spending will only rise. It’s that simple.

Enter CrowdStrike.

CrowdStrike is a leader in cybersecurity. It specializes in endpoint security, threat intelligence and cyber attack response services. They’re not just selling software; they’re selling protection that companies cannot aff

ord to lose.

CrowdStrike’s Falcon platform is built in the cloud, powered by AI, and designed to catch threats before they even become headlines. That’s why businesses from small firms to Fortune 500s are paying to protect themselves, and they keep paying. Once you’re in the CrowdStrike ecosystem, you rarely leave.

That group currently includes 300 of the Fortune 500 companies. 42 of the 50 U.S. states.

CrowdStrike is more than a software company, it’s a backbone of modern business security. With massive secular tailwinds, sticky recurring revenue, expanding opportunities, and a defensible moat. CrowdStrike isn’t just a growth stock, it’s a mission-critical one.

**The Case for CrowdStrike**

*   **Mission-Critical Spend** – Cybersecurity budgets are sticky. Companies may renegotiate SaaS contracts or trim cloud usage, but they don’t roll the dice on protection. That gives CrowdStrike unusually durable demand, even in downturns. 
*   **Best-in-Class Platform** – The Falcon platform is cloud-native and AI-driven, recognized as one of the top endpoint protection tools in the industry. 
*   **Compounding Revenue** – Subscription revenue means predictable growth. They project a $10 billion ARR goal by 2031 and $20 billion ARR projection by 2036. Over 90% of their revenue is subscription based. 

- **Retention Holding Up –** With an over 115% net retention, existing customers are expanding their usage and spending more every year.

*   **Growing Market** – From endpoint protection to cloud, identity, and XDR, CrowdStrike’s management sees a total addressable market (TAM) of $300 billion by 2029. That’s up from $116 billion this year. 
*   **Growth + Profitability** – Rare among high-growth names, CrowdStrike is GAAP profitable with strong free cash flow, giving them room to invest aggressively while still delivering to shareholders. They’ve maintained an over 73% gross profit margin. 
*   **A Data-Driven Moat** – The “threat graph” analyzes trillions of events daily. More data = better AI = better protection. This flywheel effect is incredibly hard for competitors to replicate. 

CrowdStrike pairs rapid revenue growth and high customer retention with expanding market opportunities, founder-led execution, strong profitability, and a defensible moat.

In today’s world, I feel that I to have a horse in the cybersecurity space. CrowdStrike is my horse.

It has been and is still one of my favorite long-term growth stocks in the entire stock market. I’ve been long since I started my position back in September 2020. My last sale where I trimmed my position was in January 2022.

I’ve held every share since and have continued to buy more during pullbacks.

On any market pullback, this is the first name on my buy list.

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. provides cybersecurity solutions in the United States and internationally. Its unified platform provides cloud-delivered protection of endpoints, cloud workloads, identity, and data through a software as a service (SaaS) subscription-based model. The company offers corporate endpoint and cloud workload security, managed security, security and vulnerability management, IT operations management, identity protection, threat intelligence, data protection, SaaS security posture management, and AI powered workflow automation, and securing generative AI workload services, as well as security orchestration, automation, and response; and security information and event management, and log management services. It primarily sells subscriptions to its Falcon platform and cloud modules. CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. was incorporated in 2011 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas.

The Cybersecurity Stock To Own
------------------------------

Strong Growth, Sticky Revenue, and a Critical Industry Tailwind

If you’ve been paying attention to the headlines lately, you’ll notice something, cyberattacks aren’t slowing down. In fact, they’re multiplying.

From ransomware hitting hospitals to phishing campaigns targeting Fortune 500s, the cost of being unprepared is higher than ever.

Cybersecurity isn’t getting cut. If anything, it’s the last line item on the list, spending will only rise. It’s that simple.

Enter CrowdStrike.

CrowdStrike is a leader in cybersecurity. It specializes in endpoint security, threat intelligence and cyber attack response services. They’re not just selling software; they’re selling protection that companies cannot aff

ord to lose.

CrowdStrike’s Falcon platform is built in the cloud, powered by AI, and designed to catch threats before they even become headlines. That’s why businesses from small firms to Fortune 500s are paying to protect themselves, and they keep paying. Once you’re in the CrowdStrike ecosystem, you rarely leave.

That group currently includes 300 of the Fortune 500 companies. 42 of the 50 U.S. states.

CrowdStrike is more than a software company, it’s a backbone of modern business security. With massive secular tailwinds, sticky recurring revenue, expanding opportunities, and a defensible moat. CrowdStrike isn’t just a growth stock, it’s a mission-critical one.

**The Case for CrowdStrike**

*   **Mission-Critical Spend** – Cybersecurity budgets are sticky. Companies may renegotiate SaaS contracts or trim cloud usage, but they don’t roll the dice on protection. That gives CrowdStrike unusually durable demand, even in downturns. 
*   **Best-in-Class Platform** – The Falcon platform is cloud-native and AI-driven, recognized as one of the top endpoint protection tools in the industry. 
*   **Compounding Revenue** – Subscription revenue means predictable growth. They project a $10 billion ARR goal by 2031 and $20 billion ARR projection by 2036. Over 90% of their revenue is subscription based. 

- **Retention Holding Up –** With an over 115% net retention, existing customers are expanding their usage and spending more every year.

*   **Growing Market** – From endpoint protection to cloud, identity, and XDR, CrowdStrike’s management sees a total addressable market (TAM) of $300 billion by 2029. That’s up from $116 billion this year. 
*   **Growth + Profitability** – Rare among high-growth names, CrowdStrike is GAAP profitable with strong free cash flow, giving them room to invest aggressively while still delivering to shareholders. They’ve maintained an over 73% gross profit margin. 
*   **A Data-Driven Moat** – The “threat graph” analyzes trillions of events daily. More data = better AI = better protection. This flywheel effect is incredibly hard for competitors to replicate. 

CrowdStrike pairs rapid revenue growth and high customer retention with expanding market opportunities, founder-led execution, strong profitability, and a defensible moat.

In today’s world, I feel that I to have a horse in the cybersecurity space. CrowdStrike is my horse.

It has been and is still one of my favorite long-term growth stocks in the entire stock market. I’ve been long since I started my position back in September 2020. My last sale where I trimmed my position was in January 2022.

I’ve held every share since and have continued to buy more during pullbacks.

On any market pullback, this is the first name on my buy list.

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. provides cybersecurity solutions in the United States and internationally. Its unified platform provides cloud-delivered protection of endpoints, cloud workloads, identity, and data through a software as a service (SaaS) subscription-based model. The company offers corporate endpoint and cloud workload security, managed security, security and vulnerability management, IT operations management, identity protection, threat intelligence, data protection, SaaS security posture management, and AI powered workflow automation, and securing generative AI workload services, as well as security orchestration, automation, and response; and security information and event management, and log management services. It primarily sells subscriptions to its Falcon platform and cloud modules. CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. was incorporated in 2011 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas.

The Cybersecurity Stock To Own
------------------------------

Strong Growth, Sticky Revenue, and a Critical Industry Tailwind

If you’ve been paying attention to the headlines lately, you’ll notice something, cyberattacks aren’t slowing down. In fact, they’re multiplying.

From ransomware hitting hospitals to phishing campaigns targeting Fortune 500s, the cost of being unprepared is higher than ever.

Cybersecurity isn’t getting cut. If anything, it’s the last line item on the list, spending will only rise. It’s that simple.

Enter CrowdStrike.

CrowdStrike is a leader in cybersecurity. It specializes in endpoint security, threat intelligence and cyber attack response services. They’re not just selling software; they’re selling protection that companies cannot aff

ord to lose.

CrowdStrike’s Falcon platform is built in the cloud, powered by AI, and designed to catch threats before they even become headlines. That’s why businesses from small firms to Fortune 500s are paying to protect themselves, and they keep paying. Once you’re in the CrowdStrike ecosystem, you rarely leave.

That group currently includes 300 of the Fortune 500 companies. 42 of the 50 U.S. states.

CrowdStrike is more than a software company, it’s a backbone of modern business security. With massive secular tailwinds, sticky recurring revenue, expanding opportunities, and a defensible moat. CrowdStrike isn’t just a growth stock, it’s a mission-critical one.

**The Case for CrowdStrike**

*   **Mission-Critical Spend** – Cybersecurity budgets are sticky. Companies may renegotiate SaaS contracts or trim cloud usage, but they don’t roll the dice on protection. That gives CrowdStrike unusually durable demand, even in downturns. 
*   **Best-in-Class Platform** – The Falcon platform is cloud-native and AI-driven, recognized as one of the top endpoint protection tools in the industry. 
*   **Compounding Revenue** – Subscription revenue means predictable growth. They project a $10 billion ARR goal by 2031 and $20 billion ARR projection by 2036. Over 90% of their revenue is subscription based. 

- **Retention Holding Up –** With an over 115% net retention, existing customers are expanding their usage and spending more every year.

*   **Growing Market** – From endpoint protection to cloud, identity, and XDR, CrowdStrike’s management sees a total addressable market (TAM) of $300 billion by 2029. That’s up from $116 billion this year. 
*   **Growth + Profitability** – Rare among high-growth names, CrowdStrike is GAAP profitable with strong free cash flow, giving them room to invest aggressively while still delivering to shareholders. They’ve maintained an over 73% gross profit margin. 
*   **A Data-Driven Moat** – The “threat graph” analyzes trillions of events daily. More data = better AI = better protection. This flywheel effect is incredibly hard for competitors to replicate. 

CrowdStrike pairs rapid revenue growth and high customer retention with expanding market opportunities, founder-led execution, strong profitability, and a defensible moat.

In today’s world, I feel that I to have a horse in the cybersecurity space. CrowdStrike is my horse.

It has been and is still one of my favorite long-term growth stocks in the entire stock market. I’ve been long since I started my position back in September 2020. My last sale where I trimmed my position was in January 2022.

I’ve held every share since and have continued to buy more during pullbacks.

On any market pullback, this is the first name on my buy list.

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. provides cybersecurity solutions in the United States and internationally. Its unified platform provides cloud-delivered protection of endpoints, cloud workloads, identity, and data through a software as a service (SaaS) subscription-based model. The company offers corporate endpoint and cloud workload security, managed security, security and vulnerability management, IT operations management, identity protection, threat intelligence, data protection, SaaS security posture management, and AI powered workflow automation, and securing generative AI workload services, as well as security orchestration, automation, and response; and security information and event management, and log management services. It primarily sells subscriptions to its Falcon platform and cloud modules. CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. was incorporated in 2011 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas.

The Cybersecurity Stock To Own
------------------------------

Strong Growth, Sticky Revenue, and a Critical Industry Tailwind

If you’ve been paying attention to the headlines lately, you’ll notice something, cyberattacks aren’t slowing down. In fact, they’re multiplying.

From ransomware hitting hospitals to phishing campaigns targeting Fortune 500s, the cost of being unprepared is higher than ever.

Cybersecurity isn’t getting cut. If anything, it’s the last line item on the list, spending will only rise. It’s that simple.

Enter CrowdStrike.

CrowdStrike is a leader in cybersecurity. It specializes in endpoint security, threat intelligence and cyber attack response services. They’re not just selling software; they’re selling protection that companies cannot aff

ord to lose.

CrowdStrike’s Falcon platform is built in the cloud, powered by AI, and designed to catch threats before they even become headlines. That’s why businesses from small firms to Fortune 500s are paying to protect themselves, and they keep paying. Once you’re in the CrowdStrike ecosystem, you rarely leave.

That group currently includes 300 of the Fortune 500 companies. 42 of the 50 U.S. states.

CrowdStrike is more than a software company, it’s a backbone of modern business security. With massive secular tailwinds, sticky recurring revenue, expanding opportunities, and a defensible moat. CrowdStrike isn’t just a growth stock, it’s a mission-critical one.

**The Case for CrowdStrike**

*   **Mission-Critical Spend** – Cybersecurity budgets are sticky. Companies may renegotiate SaaS contracts or trim cloud usage, but they don’t roll the dice on protection. That gives CrowdStrike unusually durable demand, even in downturns. 
*   **Best-in-Class Platform** – The Falcon platform is cloud-native and AI-driven, recognized as one of the top endpoint protection tools in the industry. 
*   **Compounding Revenue** – Subscription revenue means predictable growth. They project a $10 billion ARR goal by 2031 and $20 billion ARR projection by 2036. Over 90% of their revenue is subscription based. 

- **Retention Holding Up –** With an over 115% net retention, existing customers are expanding their usage and spending more every year.

*   **Growing Market** – From endpoint protection to cloud, identity, and XDR, CrowdStrike’s management sees a total addressable market (TAM) of $300 billion by 2029. That’s up from $116 billion this year. 
*   **Growth + Profitability** – Rare among high-growth names, CrowdStrike is GAAP profitable with strong free cash flow, giving them room to invest aggressively while still delivering to shareholders. They’ve maintained an over 73% gross profit margin. 
*   **A Data-Driven Moat** – The “threat graph” analyzes trillions of events daily. More data = better AI = better protection. This flywheel effect is incredibly hard for competitors to replicate. 

CrowdStrike pairs rapid revenue growth and high customer retention with expanding market opportunities, founder-led execution, strong profitability, and a defensible moat.

In today’s world, I feel that I to have a horse in the cybersecurity space. CrowdStrike is my horse.

It has been and is still one of my favorite long-term growth stocks in the entire stock market. I’ve been long since I started my position back in September 2020. My last sale where I trimmed my position was in January 2022.

I’ve held every share since and have continued to buy more during pullbacks.

On any market pullback, this is the first name on my buy list.

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. provides cybersecurity solutions in the United States and internationally. Its unified platform provides cloud-delivered protection of endpoints, cloud workloads, identity, and data through a software as a service (SaaS) subscription-based model. The company offers corporate endpoint and cloud workload security, managed security, security and vulnerability management, IT operations management, identity protection, threat intelligence, data protection, SaaS security posture management, and AI powered workflow automation, and securing generative AI workload services, as well as security orchestration, automation, and response; and security information and event management, and log management services. It primarily sells subscriptions to its Falcon platform and cloud modules. CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. was incorporated in 2011 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas.

The Cybersecurity Stock To Own
------------------------------

Strong Growth, Sticky Revenue, and a Critical Industry Tailwind

If you’ve been paying attention to the headlines lately, you’ll notice something, cyberattacks aren’t slowing down. In fact, they’re multiplying.

From ransomware hitting hospitals to phishing campaigns targeting Fortune 500s, the cost of being unprepared is higher than ever.

Cybersecurity isn’t getting cut. If anything, it’s the last line item on the list, spending will only rise. It’s that simple.

Enter CrowdStrike.

CrowdStrike is a leader in cybersecurity. It specializes in endpoint security, threat intelligence and cyber attack response services. They’re not just selling software; they’re selling protection that companies cannot aff

ord to lose.

CrowdStrike’s Falcon platform is built in the cloud, powered by AI, and designed to catch threats before they even become headlines. That’s why businesses from small firms to Fortune 500s are paying to protect themselves, and they keep paying. Once you’re in the CrowdStrike ecosystem, you rarely leave.

That group currently includes 300 of the Fortune 500 companies. 42 of the 50 U.S. states.

CrowdStrike is more than a software company, it’s a backbone of modern business security. With massive secular tailwinds, sticky recurring revenue, expanding opportunities, and a defensible moat. CrowdStrike isn’t just a growth stock, it’s a mission-critical one.

**The Case for CrowdStrike**

*   **Mission-Critical Spend** – Cybersecurity budgets are sticky. Companies may renegotiate SaaS contracts or trim cloud usage, but they don’t roll the dice on protection. That gives CrowdStrike unusually durable demand, even in downturns. 
*   **Best-in-Class Platform** – The Falcon platform is cloud-native and AI-driven, recognized as one of the top endpoint protection tools in the industry. 
*   **Compounding Revenue** – Subscription revenue means predictable growth. They project a $10 billion ARR goal by 2031 and $20 billion ARR projection by 2036. Over 90% of their revenue is subscription based. 

- **Retention Holding Up –** With an over 115% net retention, existing customers are expanding their usage and spending more every year.

*   **Growing Market** – From endpoint protection to cloud, identity, and XDR, CrowdStrike’s management sees a total addressable market (TAM) of $300 billion by 2029. That’s up from $116 billion this year. 
*   **Growth + Profitability** – Rare among high-growth names, CrowdStrike is GAAP profitable with strong free cash flow, giving them room to invest aggressively while still delivering to shareholders. They’ve maintained an over 73% gross profit margin. 
*   **A Data-Driven Moat** – The “threat graph” analyzes trillions of events daily. More data = better AI = better protection. This flywheel effect is incredibly hard for competitors to replicate. 

CrowdStrike pairs rapid revenue growth and high customer retention with expanding market opportunities, founder-led execution, strong profitability, and a defensible moat.

In today’s world, I feel that I to have a horse in the cybersecurity space. CrowdStrike is my horse.

It has been and is still one of my favorite long-term growth stocks in the entire stock market. I’ve been long since I started my position back in September 2020. My last sale where I trimmed my position was in January 2022.

I’ve held every share since and have continued to buy more during pullbacks.

On any market pullback, this is the first name on my buy list.

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. provides cybersecurity solutions in the United States and internationally. Its unified platform provides cloud-delivered protection of endpoints, cloud workloads, identity, and data through a software as a service (SaaS) subscription-based model. The company offers corporate endpoint and cloud workload security, managed security, security and vulnerability management, IT operations management, identity protection, threat intelligence, data protection, SaaS security posture management, and AI powered workflow automation, and securing generative AI workload services, as well as security orchestration, automation, and response; and security information and event management, and log management services. It primarily sells subscriptions to its Falcon platform and cloud modules. CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. was incorporated in 2011 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas.

The Cybersecurity Stock To Own
------------------------------

Strong Growth, Sticky Revenue, and a Critical Industry Tailwind

If you’ve been paying attention to the headlines lately, you’ll notice something, cyberattacks aren’t slowing down. In fact, they’re multiplying.

From ransomware hitting hospitals to phishing campaigns targeting Fortune 500s, the cost of being unprepared is higher than ever.

Cybersecurity isn’t getting cut. If anything, it’s the last line item on the list, spending will only rise. It’s that simple.

Enter CrowdStrike.

CrowdStrike is a leader in cybersecurity. It specializes in endpoint security, threat intelligence and cyber attack response services. They’re not just selling software; they’re selling protection that companies cannot aff

ord to lose.

CrowdStrike’s Falcon platform is built in the cloud, powered by AI, and designed to catch threats before they even become headlines. That’s why businesses from small firms to Fortune 500s are paying to protect themselves, and they keep paying. Once you’re in the CrowdStrike ecosystem, you rarely leave.

That group currently includes 300 of the Fortune 500 companies. 42 of the 50 U.S. states.

CrowdStrike is more than a software company, it’s a backbone of modern business security. With massive secular tailwinds, sticky recurring revenue, expanding opportunities, and a defensible moat. CrowdStrike isn’t just a growth stock, it’s a mission-critical one.

**The Case for CrowdStrike**

*   **Mission-Critical Spend** – Cybersecurity budgets are sticky. Companies may renegotiate SaaS contracts or trim cloud usage, but they don’t roll the dice on protection. That gives CrowdStrike unusually durable demand, even in downturns. 
*   **Best-in-Class Platform** – The Falcon platform is cloud-native and AI-driven, recognized as one of the top endpoint protection tools in the industry. 
*   **Compounding Revenue** – Subscription revenue means predictable growth. They project a $10 billion ARR goal by 2031 and $20 billion ARR projection by 2036. Over 90% of their revenue is subscription based. 

- **Retention Holding Up –** With an over 115% net retention, existing customers are expanding their usage and spending more every year.

*   **Growing Market** – From endpoint protection to cloud, identity, and XDR, CrowdStrike’s management sees a total addressable market (TAM) of $300 billion by 2029. That’s up from $116 billion this year. 
*   **Growth + Profitability** – Rare among high-growth names, CrowdStrike is GAAP profitable with strong free cash flow, giving them room to invest aggressively while still delivering to shareholders. They’ve maintained an over 73% gross profit margin. 
*   **A Data-Driven Moat** – The “threat graph” analyzes trillions of events daily. More data = better AI = better protection. This flywheel effect is incredibly hard for competitors to replicate. 

CrowdStrike pairs rapid revenue growth and high customer retention with expanding market opportunities, founder-led execution, strong profitability, and a defensible moat.

In today’s world, I feel that I to have a horse in the cybersecurity space. CrowdStrike is my horse.

It has been and is still one of my favorite long-term growth stocks in the entire stock market. I’ve been long since I started my position back in September 2020. My last sale where I trimmed my position was in January 2022.

I’ve held every share since and have continued to buy more during pullbacks.

On any market pullback, this is the first name on my buy list.

# CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) Tops Q3 Earnings and Revenue Estimates

Zacks Equity Research

3 min read

In this article:  

[CRWD

+2.46%](/quote/CRWD/ "CRWD")

CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) came out with quarterly earnings of $0.96 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.94 per share. This compares to earnings of $0.93 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +2.13%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this cloud-based security company would post earnings of $0.83 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.93, delivering a surprise of +12.05%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

CrowdStrike, which belongs to the Zacks Security industry, posted revenues of $1.23 billion for the quarter ended October 2025, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 1.61%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $1.01 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates three times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

CrowdStrike shares have added about 47.3% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 15.8%.

## What's Next for CrowdStrike?

While CrowdStrike has outperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for CrowdStrike was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $1.09 on $1.29 billion in revenues for the coming quarter and $3.67 on $4.78 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Investors should be mindful of the fact that the outlook for the industry can have a material impact on the performance of the stock as well. In terms of the Zacks Industry Rank, Security is currently in the top 24% of the 250 plus Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

DocuSign (DOCU), another stock in the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector, has yet to report results for the quarter ended October 2025. The results are expected to be released on December 4.

This provider of electronic signature technology is expected to post quarterly earnings of $0.92 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +2.2%. The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has remained unchanged over the last 30 days.

DocuSign's revenues are expected to be $806.13 million, up 6.8% from the year-ago quarter.

# CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) Tops Q3 Earnings and Revenue Estimates

Zacks Equity Research

3 min read

In this article:  

[CRWD

+2.46%](/quote/CRWD/ "CRWD")

CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) came out with quarterly earnings of $0.96 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.94 per share. This compares to earnings of $0.93 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +2.13%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this cloud-based security company would post earnings of $0.83 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.93, delivering a surprise of +12.05%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

CrowdStrike, which belongs to the Zacks Security industry, posted revenues of $1.23 billion for the quarter ended October 2025, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 1.61%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $1.01 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates three times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

CrowdStrike shares have added about 47.3% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 15.8%.

## What's Next for CrowdStrike?

While CrowdStrike has outperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for CrowdStrike was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $1.09 on $1.29 billion in revenues for the coming quarter and $3.67 on $4.78 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Investors should be mindful of the fact that the outlook for the industry can have a material impact on the performance of the stock as well. In terms of the Zacks Industry Rank, Security is currently in the top 24% of the 250 plus Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

DocuSign (DOCU), another stock in the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector, has yet to report results for the quarter ended October 2025. The results are expected to be released on December 4.

This provider of electronic signature technology is expected to post quarterly earnings of $0.92 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +2.2%. The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has remained unchanged over the last 30 days.

DocuSign's revenues are expected to be $806.13 million, up 6.8% from the year-ago quarter.

# CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) Tops Q3 Earnings and Revenue Estimates

Zacks Equity Research

3 min read

In this article:  

[CRWD

+2.46%](/quote/CRWD/ "CRWD")

CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) came out with quarterly earnings of $0.96 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.94 per share. This compares to earnings of $0.93 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +2.13%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this cloud-based security company would post earnings of $0.83 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.93, delivering a surprise of +12.05%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

CrowdStrike, which belongs to the Zacks Security industry, posted revenues of $1.23 billion for the quarter ended October 2025, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 1.61%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $1.01 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates three times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

CrowdStrike shares have added about 47.3% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 15.8%.

## What's Next for CrowdStrike?

While CrowdStrike has outperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

# CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) Tops Q3 Earnings and Revenue Estimates

Zacks Equity Research

3 min read

In this article:  

[CRWD

+2.46%](/quote/CRWD/ "CRWD")

CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) came out with quarterly earnings of $0.96 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.94 per share. This compares to earnings of $0.93 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +2.13%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this cloud-based security company would post earnings of $0.83 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.93, delivering a surprise of +12.05%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

CrowdStrike, which belongs to the Zacks Security industry, posted revenues of $1.23 billion for the quarter ended October 2025, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 1.61%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $1.01 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates three times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

CrowdStrike shares have added about 47.3% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 15.8%.

## What's Next for CrowdStrike?

While CrowdStrike has outperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for CrowdStrike was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $1.09 on $1.29 billion in revenues for the coming quarter and $3.67 on $4.78 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Investors should be mindful of the fact that the outlook for the industry can have a material impact on the performance of the stock as well. In terms of the Zacks Industry Rank, Security is currently in the top 24% of the 250 plus Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

DocuSign (DOCU), another stock in the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector, has yet to report results for the quarter ended October 2025. The results are expected to be released on December 4.

This provider of electronic signature technology is expected to post quarterly earnings of $0.92 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +2.2%. The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has remained unchanged over the last 30 days.

DocuSign's revenues are expected to be $806.13 million, up 6.8% from the year-ago quarter.

# CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) Tops Q3 Earnings and Revenue Estimates

Zacks Equity Research

3 min read

In this article:  

[CRWD

+2.46%](/quote/CRWD/ "CRWD")

CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) came out with quarterly earnings of $0.96 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.94 per share. This compares to earnings of $0.93 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +2.13%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this cloud-based security company would post earnings of $0.83 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.93, delivering a surprise of +12.05%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

CrowdStrike, which belongs to the Zacks Security industry, posted revenues of $1.23 billion for the quarter ended October 2025, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 1.61%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $1.01 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates three times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

CrowdStrike shares have added about 47.3% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 15.8%.

## What's Next for CrowdStrike?

While CrowdStrike has outperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for CrowdStrike was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $1.09 on $1.29 billion in revenues for the coming quarter and $3.67 on $4.78 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Investors should be mindful of the fact that the outlook for the industry can have a material impact on the performance of the stock as well. In terms of the Zacks Industry Rank, Security is currently in the top 24% of the 250 plus Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

DocuSign (DOCU), another stock in the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector, has yet to report results for the quarter ended October 2025. The results are expected to be released on December 4.

This provider of electronic signature technology is expected to post quarterly earnings of $0.92 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +2.2%. The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has remained unchanged over the last 30 days.

DocuSign's revenues are expected to be $806.13 million, up 6.8% from the year-ago quarter.

# CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) Tops Q3 Earnings and Revenue Estimates

Zacks Equity Research

3 min read

In this article:  

[CRWD

+2.46%](/quote/CRWD/ "CRWD")

CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) came out with quarterly earnings of $0.96 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.94 per share. This compares to earnings of $0.93 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +2.13%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this cloud-based security company would post earnings of $0.83 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.93, delivering a surprise of +12.05%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

CrowdStrike, which belongs to the Zacks Security industry, posted revenues of $1.23 billion for the quarter ended October 2025, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 1.61%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $1.01 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates three times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

CrowdStrike shares have added about 47.3% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 15.8%.

## What's Next for CrowdStrike?

While CrowdStrike has outperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for CrowdStrike was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $1.09 on $1.29 billion in revenues for the coming quarter and $3.67 on $4.78 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Investors should be mindful of the fact that the outlook for the industry can have a material impact on the performance of the stock as well. In terms of the Zacks Industry Rank, Security is currently in the top 24% of the 250 plus Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

DocuSign (DOCU), another stock in the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector, has yet to report results for the quarter ended October 2025. The results are expected to be released on December 4.

This provider of electronic signature technology is expected to post quarterly earnings of $0.92 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +2.2%. The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has remained unchanged over the last 30 days.

DocuSign's revenues are expected to be $806.13 million, up 6.8% from the year-ago quarter.

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. Overview Software - Infrastructure / Technology
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. provides cybersecurity solutions in the United States and internationally. Its unified platform provides cloud-delivered protection of endpoints, cloud workloads, identity, and data through a software as a service (SaaS) subscription-based model. The company offers corporate endpoint and cloud workload security, managed security, security and vulnerability management, IT operations management, identity protection, threat intelligence, data protection, SaaS security posture management, and AI powered workflow automation, and securing generative AI workload services, as well as security orchestration, automation, and response; and security information and event management, and log management services. It primarily sells subscriptions to its Falcon platform and cloud modules. CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. was incorporated in 2011 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas.
